daily.title: India's FY28 fiscal deficit projected to stay unchanged at 4.3% of GDP: Deutsche Bank
daily.summary: Deutsche Bank projects India's FY28 deficit at 4.3% of GDP despite rising pay, subsidies, and oil costs. "The central government will most likely meet its FY27 fiscal deficit target of 4.3% of GDP; however, FY28 consolidation looks considerably more challenging. Considering the various risks, we forecast the FY28 fiscal deficit to remain unchanged at 4.3% of GDP," the report stated. Several cushions support the government's fiscal math in the current fiscal year, including a substantial Reserve Bank of India dividend of ₹2.9 lakh crore, an ₹1 lakh crore Economic Stabilisation Fund provision, potential capital expenditure compression, and higher-than-expected disinvestment receipts.…

daily.title: The evolving dairy-agriculture ecosystem: Strengthening rural livelihoods and India’s food economy
daily.summary: Strengthening India's rural economy: dairy-led growth boosts livelihoods, productivity, and food security through inclusive markets and innovation. Agriculture and dairying are not parallel activities; they are integral to one rural economy. Farming income follows the calendar. It arrives after the harvest and has to stretch until the next one. Dairying runs on a different clock, bringing in money from routine milk sales throughout the year. The field brings a large seasonal income, and the cowshed brings steady, dependable cash that keeps the household running between harvests and acts as a cushion when weather or prices turn.

daily.title: Supreme Court Allows Appeal in Income Tax Exemption Case for Co-operative Society. The Court ruled that profits from transactions with non-members are exempt under Section 60 of the Income-tax Act, 1922.

RBI Sets ₹100 Crore Net Worth for White-Label ATM Operators
breaking.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued the Reserve Bank of India (White Label ATM Operators) Directions, 2026, on 27 November 2026. The directions took effect immediately Non-bank entities seeking to set up, own and operate White Label ATMs (WLAs) must obtain authorisation under the RBI’s Master Direction on Authorisation to operate a Payment System, dated 15 June 2026. They must maintain a minimum net worth of ₹100 crore at all times. White Label ATM Operators (WLAOs) must maintain a deployment ratio of at least 1:2:3 across metro or urban, semi-urban and rural centres, respectively.

RBI rolls back liquidity-tightening measure as credit growth outpaces deposits
breaking.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) eases liquidity-tightening measures, reducing the daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) requirement to 90% as banks face mounting pressure from surging credit demand and slower deposit growth The earlier measure was aimed at absorbing surplus liquidity generated by inflows under the special Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) or FCNR(B) deposit scheme. The decision comes at a time when banks are struggling to keep pace with rising credit demand as deposit mobilisation remains slower. In the fortnight ended November 15, 2026, bank credit grew 19.3% year-on-year, while deposits increased by 16.4%.

breaking.title: RBI needs to Revisit the terminology used by it and banks: Non-Callable Bank Fixed Deposits with no-premature closure facility

Everyone who has invested in a bulk bank fixed deposit (FD) understands two basic things: the interest the deposit will earn and the period for which the money will remain invested. There is, however, a third equally important consideration: can the depositor get the money back before maturity if an unexpected financial need arises?

breaking.summary: MUMBAI: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has allowed foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to participate in non-cash, physically settled non-agri The move follows deliberations by the Commodity Derivatives Advisory Committee and public consultations. breaking.title: Many FTA benefits untapped: RBI
breaking.summary: Indian exporters are leaving much of the benefit of the country’s expanding free-trade network untapped, with only 20-30% of eligible shipments using preferential tariffs against 60-70% in partner countries, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said. As a result, 70-80% of eligible Indian exports continue to enter partner markets under regular most-favoured-nation (MFN) tariffs, making them less competitive than goods from countries that use trade agreements more effectively.

breaking.title: RBI Clubs 25 Card Payment Circulars Into A Single Framework
breaking.summary: The RBI has clubbed 25 existing circulars, governing debit, credit and prepaid card transactions, under a single regulatory framework. Called the Reserve Bank of India (Digital Payments – Card-based transaction) Directions, 2026 , the new norms look to streamline compliance and security rules for card-based digital payments. The new rules also replace the need for referring multiple instructions issued over the years. The new framework, which comes into force with immediate effect, primarily pertains to banks, non-bank payment system providers, and ecosystem participants under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act.
